scope: Exact pinned stable-worldmodel RGB implementations and saved benchmark configurations only. CPU_ONLY is not a claim about all versions, forks, or future backends.

upstream.proof: Every copied SWM .py file byte-compared with git show at pinned commit; source_hashes.json records SHA256.

swm/AcrobotControl-v1.notes: Pinned RGB path draws pygame/gfxdraw primitives into software pygame.Surface, then pygame.surfarray.pixels3d. SWM wrapper applies NumPy color replacements. No CUDA/OpenGL renderer selection in this call path. Human display acceleration would not accelerate these surface rasterization calls.

swm/TwoRoom-v1.evidence: source/stable_worldmodel/envs/two_room/env.py:282; source_hashes.json; supplemental/results/40/result.json: source CUDA execution verified on RTX A5500; 3090 timings pending
swm/TwoRoom-v1.notes: No constructor device argument. Unchanged upstream Torch rasterizer is configured by moving source-owned tensor buffers to CUDA and rendering under torch.device(cuda). Public render still copies image to CPU NumPy; that copy stays timed. No raster math replaced. Benchmark scopes the accepted saved default configurations, not all possible variations.

swm/Piecewise-v0.evidence: source/stable_worldmodel/envs/piecewise/piecewise_env.py:260; source_hashes.json; supplemental/results/34/result.json: source CUDA execution verified on RTX A5500; 3090 timings pending
swm/Piecewise-v0.notes: No constructor device argument. Unchanged upstream Torch rasterizer is configured by moving source-owned tensor buffers to CUDA and rendering under torch.device(cuda). Public render still copies image to CPU NumPy; that copy stays timed. No raster math replaced. Benchmark scopes the accepted saved default configurations, not all possible variations. Optional render_bias_field uses Matplotlib on CPU and is outside the audited default configuration; this audit makes no general all-GPU claim for that variation.

runtime_gate.source_gpu_configuration: Source-owned Torch buffers moved outside timers; same public source render under torch.device(cuda), including its .cpu().numpy() output path. CUDA output destination adds upload for source and preserves existing paired contract.
runtime_gate.source_cpu_gpu_gap: source_anchor_mse in results compares CUDA-source pixels against saved CPU-source oracle pixels at identical State; not a same-allocation CPU-vs-GPU timing ratio.
